title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Standards, templates, and operating procedures for developer-facing documentation managed by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team. Covers SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical fixes for top support issues.
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the standards and operating procedures for all Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation that ships to Redwood customers and internal users. It consolidates guidance for: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures (content lifecycle, releases, and health), and the canonical fixes for the top support issues reported to DevEx.

Goals:
- Provide consistent, high-quality developer documentation that minimizes support friction and accelerates time-to-value for customers.
- Reduce duplicate or stale content through a documented lifecycle and ownership model.
- Capture canonical fixes for the most common support issues to enable faster TTR (time-to-resolution).

Scope:
- Public-facing and internal docs produced by DevEx: SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go), quickstarts, API examples, and docs-site procedures.
- Does NOT cover product PRD content, legal templates, or deep research notebooks (those live in other spaces).

Document structure and canonical templates:
1) Page layout (required for SDK guides and quickstarts):
  - H1: short descriptive title (e.g., "Python SDK Quickstart: Text Generation")
  - Short intro (1-3 sentences): what the page covers and expected outcome
  - Prerequisites: list versions, accounts, environment variables, CLI tools
  - Step-by-step quickstart: numbered commands with expected output snippets
  - API reference snippet: minimal example showing function/endpoint usage
  - Troubleshooting section: top 3 issues specific to this page
  - Links: related pages and SDK reference docs

2) SDK guide template (file header metadata required):
  - Title
  - Overview / When to use this SDK
  - Supported versions and compatibility matrix (table)
  - Installation instructions (pip/npm/go install)
  - Auth and configuration examples (env vars and sample config JSON)
  - Common patterns and recipes (streaming, batching, function calling)
  - Migration notes for breaking changes
  - Tests / example apps (links to GitHub samples)
  - Ownership and contact (DevEx owner and on-call)

Quickstarts and templates (guidance):
- Quickstarts must be end-to-end and runnable in <10 minutes on a developer laptop or cloud sandbox. Include copy-paste commands and minimal dependencies.
- Provide one canonical quickstart per major flow: Text generation, Chat (stateful), Embeddings, and Reranking. Each quickstart must include:
  1. TL;DR (2-3 lines) with expected output
  2. Prereqs and environment setup
  3. Step-by-step commands and short code snippets
  4. Cleanup commands
  5. Links to SDK reference and sample repo

- Template repositories: all templates must include a README, CI check that validates the quickstart run, and a LICENSE matching Redwood norms. Template owners must ensure templates are runnable and updated with SDK releases.

API examples (guidance and style):
- Examples should be minimal, idiomatic, and focused on a single concept. Prefer full-file examples (e.g., python/example_generate.py) over one-liners.
- Each example must contain:
  - A single sentence describing the example goal
  - Required imports and authentication block
  - Input example and expected output snippet as a comment
  - Error handling example for the most common failure mode

Example: Python generation snippet (canonical):
# python/example_generate.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-1', prompt='Write a haiku about observability')
print(resp.text)

Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle):
- Content stages: draft -> in_review -> published -> deprecated
- Ownership: every page must declare an owner (person) and an owner_team label. Owners are responsible for responding to doc issues and keeping content accurate.
- Review process: PRs go to repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site; include: changelog entry, test run (link to CI job), and reviewers list. After 2 approvals, content automatically gets staged to the preview site.
- Release cadence: weekly content deploys (Tues 02:00 UTC). Critical fixes can be hotfixed with an expedited review and must include a rollback plan.
- Health checks and maintenance: monthly audit to find docs with >180 days since last_updated; owners get automated Slack reminders. Pages failing the audit must either be updated, redirected, or archived.

Operational runbook for docs incidents:
1) Symptom: site build failing or preview deploy failing
2) Owner: DevEx infra on-call (@devex-infra)
3) Steps:
   a) Check CI: github actions build logs -> common fail strings (missing dependency, broken markdown frontmatter)
   b) Revert recent PRs if build started failing immediately after a merge
   c) Run local build: yarn build && yarn start --preview to reproduce
   d) If external, open incident in PagerDuty and post status to #docs-status

Top support issues and canonical fixes (high-impact, high-frequency):
- Issue 1: Authentication errors from new users (401 / invalid API key)
  Canonical fix:
  1) Confirm API key present: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`
  2) Ensure key is marked with required scopes in Console (billing/usage vs admin scopes)
  3) If using private deployment, confirm control plane URL and CORS settings
  4) If still failing, ask for full curl trace and client SDK logs (enable DEBUG)
- Issue 2: Streaming responses are truncated or stall
  Canonical fix:
  1) Ensure client uses streaming endpoint and supports chunked transfer
  2) Check proxy/load balancer config for request/response timeouts (recommended >120s)
  3) Validate model selection and max_tokens vs client-side buffer sizes
- Issue 3: High latency for short requests
  Canonical fix:
  1) Check routing policy used (latency vs cost) and fallback evidence in request trace
  2) Verify batching configuration or prefix cache is not causing head-of-line blocking
  3) Recommend model variant with lower cold-start times or adjust request placement (region)
- Issue 4: Embedding mismatches / inconsistent vectors
  Canonical fix:
  1) Confirm embedding model and version (many embedding regressions are model-version related)
  2) Verify normalization and pre-tokenization steps in the client are not altering input (trim/normalize whitespace)
  3) Record exact input + model_id + timestamp and escalate to Applied ML if reproduction occurs

Owner and escalation matrix:
- Primary owner: DevEx content team (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owner: DevEx platform (@devex-infra)
- For unresolved content disputes or technical inaccuracies, escalate to: Senior Docs Manager (Jorge Martinez) -> Head of Developer Experience (Li Wei) -> CTO for policy-level decisions.

Metrics and SLOs for documentation health:
- SLO: 95% of public quickstarts execute successfully in CI within 10 minutes (measured weekly)
- SLO: <7 day average time-to-first-response for doc issues filed in GitHub repo
- KPI: Number of support tickets linked to docs per month (target reduction of 20% YoY)

Maintenance checklist (quarterly):
- Audit SDK pages for version compatibility and update compatibility matrix
- Run quickstart CI on the latest SDK release and fix any regressions
- Review top 10 doc pages by traffic and ensure canonical fixes are present

Appendix A - Example frontmatter and quickstart checklist (copyable):
---
title: "Python SDK Quickstart: Text Generation"
owners: "Aisha Patel"
owner_team: "engineering"
status: "published"
labels: ["quickstart","python","sdk"]
---

Quickstart checklist:
- [ ] Can be completed in <10 minutes on a dev laptop
- [ ] CI job exists and passes
- [ ] README includes cleanup instructions
- [ ] At least one reviewer from DevEx approved

Appendix B - Sample troubleshooting command snippets:
- Reproduce auth error (curl):
curl -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hello"}'

- Local docs build:
git checkout main
git pull origin main
yarn install
yarn build
yarn start --preview

Contacts and escalation links:
- DevEx Slack channel: #devex-docs
- Docs repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site (PR template enforces frontmatter)
- Incident channel: #docs-status
